finalists.label: Pheochromocytoma
finalists.why: The presence of an enhanced left-adrenal heterogeneous mass and the patient's history of hypertension make this candidate the strongest in its group.

finalists.label: Acute Coronary Syndrome
finalists.why: The sudden-onset chest pain and elevated high-sensitivity troponin I make this candidate the strongest in its group, despite normal coronary arteries.

finalists.label: Hypertensive emergency
finalists.why: The history of hypertension and elevated white blood cell count make this candidate the strongest in its group, despite normal blood pressure at presentation.

frontier_selector.why: The presence of an adrenal mass and the patient's presentation with chest pain, tachycardia, and elevated troponin and brain-type natriuretic peptide levels, which are consistent with catecholamine excess, make Pheochromocytoma the most likely diagnosis.
